More economical and environmental alternative to calling the Maytag man - My dishwasher is on an uninsulated (and uninsulatable, if that's a word) outside wall of my kitchen, and unfortunately, my dishwasher pump motor has frozen several times (when the weather has been extremely cold) since I bought it in 2002, causing the dishwasher pump motor to fail. While it's annoying that the only permanent answer to this problem would be to remodel my kitchen, I am extremely grateful that in the meantime, this part is available and it's something that many homeowners can replace themselves. I believe that. for environmental reasons, major appliances should last for decades and be repaired (instead of replaced) whenever possible. Unfortunately, in my area at least, calling someone to repair a major appliance costs half as much as the replacing the appliance, and in some cases costs the same as replacing the appliance with a low-end model. For this reason, most people just replace their appliances when anything goes wrong, and I don't blame them. However, repairing an appliance saves money, energy (the energy to manufacture a replace, the energy to ship to the point of sale, and the energy to transport it to the place where it will be installed, the energy to cart away the old appliance, and the energy to to recycle the old appliance), and greenhouse gases.

As for the part, it was easily installed in my KitchenAid dishwasher (the hard part was pulling out the dishwasher), and has been working like a charm for over two years,

It lacks any form of plumbing, but the water receptacle is plenty big. If anything I wish that the ice basket were larger to allow it to essentially fill around the same time as the water runs out. The other quirk is that the ice comes out wet and just barely frozen. If you put into a freezer, it will stick to other ice and make a block of ice. Made in China. Have realistic expectations. - Saying that this ice machine can produce 26# of ice is a little “unrealistic”. Can it produce that much in that amount of time? Probably. . . But. . . It means that someone has to be willing to empty the small ice bin when it fills. . . and keep the water reservoir filled . . .continually. . .for 24-hours. Again. . . Unrealistic.

The small ice bin holds no more than a pound of ice. . . if that. When full, the basket fills my 32oz water bottle about 2/3 full. The inside is not at freezing temperature. So . . .Unless you remove the ice, and place it in your regular freezer, the ice will simply melt. . . and then get reprocessed. The machine will stop making ice when it fills. If you remove the ice from the container, and place it in your freezer, it will then freeze together. So you will have to break it apart.

Don’t get me wrong. . . For what it is. . . I like it. But you just have to make sure your expectations meet what this ice machine will actually do.

Quality washi tape in a great range of colors - I am delving more and move into the crafting world. A year ago I didn't know what washi tape was. It isn't top of the line, but I have bought a lot worse! The tapes come in the standarad 15mm width, and have a good amount on each roll (10 m or about 11 yards). The colors are as shown - so true to picture. I found that they generally stick quite well, with the tape ones (non-foil) sticking better than the foil colors. The tape also tears easily from the roll, but doesn't rip or shred down the roll like some cheap washi does.
One roll (the red, white & blue) did have a "tacky / gummy" feel to it that I didn't like, and that one did not re-position as well as the others. I don't know exactly why or if it was a flaw with that color. The others were fine. The foil colors seemed a little less adhesive but nothing that would stop me from using this tape.
Overall this set of washi tape is bright & vivid, sticks & repositions well, is of a quite good quality and not that cheap plastic type of tape that is just awful to work with. I would buy it again and for the price - I am very happy.

We had the idler pulley wheel fail on our Maytag dryer model number SDG3606AWW. For those unaware Whirlpool has purchased Maytag animana and is now manufacturing the replacement parts for these units so you will find multiple part numbers weather there are a Whirlpool number a Maytag number or an Amana number that are all the exact same part. For example, this part was sold under Whirlpool part wpy 54414 but it's also listed as part# AP6024203(likely the AP stands for Amana even though the product is a Maytag).
This machine is over a decade old and the only repairs it's required so far was a new belt a few year back and now this pully wheel. We decided to replace the belt (part# wp40111201 AKA part # AP6009126) while we were in there as it had some cracks starting and we might as well save ourselves the hassle.
The pully did NOT come with either the washer or microscopic retaining clip but that's okay as our old ones were still in great condition.
It also doesn't come with installation instructions (super simple, washer threaded onto post of idler arm, add pully wheel, second washer, and then retaining clip) for the pulley itself or how the belt should be rethreaded onto the pulley wheel or the motor mount. YouTube will be your friend for putting the belt on properly, check multiple videos to find the one that works best for you.
This repair was relatively quick (for a gas unit you will be doing the threading blind, check youtube to see what I mean) and seems to have resolved the issues.
Just remember, always unplug your electrical connections and in the case of gas dryers like ours, simply shut off the natural gas valve at the back of the until as well until the repair is completed.
